evals.prompt: Create a small skill called git-prune that explains our preferred safe workflow for pruning local merged branches.
evals.expected_output: A concise SKILL.md with minimal frontmatter, a specific trigger description, and no unnecessary references or scripts.
assertions: The proposed skill uses name and description frontmatter
The body omits empty boilerplate sections
The description says when to use the skill

evals.prompt: Update the csv-report skill, scripts and references. In this session the agent has repeatedly run the same three commands to normalize CSV headers, validate row counts, and emit a JSON summary, and has repeatedly pasted the same column-mapping notes before editing.
evals.expected_output: A review of the existing skill that treats scripts and references as scoped candidate reviews, then creates or proposes either artifact only if the repeated command chain or repeated context is durable and worth maintaining.
assertions: The response treats scripts and references as candidate reviews rather than automatic requirements
The recommendation uses current-session repeated tool calls or repeated context as evidence
The response can reject script or reference creation if the pattern is not durable

evals.prompt: Audit my skills for cleanup: there are two nearly identical PDF skills and one old hidden draft skill I might delete.
evals.expected_output: A cleanup plan that verifies the loaded/kept copy before deletion, preserves useful trigger nouns, and asks before deleting private or untracked skill directories.
assertions: The response audits loaded or kept copies before deletion
The response suggests cleanup before applying destructive changes
The response preserves useful trigger nouns when compacting descriptions

evals.prompt: Create a small wrapper skill called deploy-preview-review that mostly runs dev-grilling with deployment-review context and a short checklist.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation for a thin orchestrator skill that delegates to the reusable discipline instead of copying the full dev-grilling procedure into a sibling skill.
assertions: The response names the thin-orchestrator principle for wrapper skills
The response prefers a short wrapper over copied boilerplate from the underlying skill
The response preserves reusable discipline in the underlying skill rather than duplicating it

evals.prompt: A skill has a strong name and description but sets disableModelInvocation: true. Natural-language requests never load it, while an explicit slash-command wrapper does and the skill then executes correctly. Diagnose and refine the setup.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that separates filesystem existence, model discoverability, explicit wrapper transport, and post-load execution; manual invocation remains a deliberate choice rather than being replaced with alwaysApply.
assertions: The response distinguishes skill existence from loaded or live activation
The response explains that disabled model invocation prevents natural-language auto-loading
The response treats the slash-command wrapper as an explicit invocation transport
The response evaluates execution behavior only after the skill is loaded
The response rejects alwaysApply as the automatic fix

evals.prompt: Expose one reusable release-check process through an OMP skill invocation and a Grok CLI slash invocation without maintaining two versions of the workflow.
evals.expected_output: One portable Agent Skills body containing the process, with only thin harness transport adapters where needed and separate discovery/invocation checks for each host.
assertions: The response keeps one reusable SKILL.md body as the process source of truth
The response limits harness adapters to discovery, invocation, or metadata differences
The response does not duplicate the operational process across OMP and Grok CLI
The response prefers each host's native skill invocation before creating a wrapper
The response verifies discovery, invocation timing, and post-load behavior per transport

evals.prompt: /skill:create-surface-verification-adapter has already established eligibility and received exact approve for an unchanged proposal. Author only the supplied adapter root and file manifest from its caller-owned tuple, then return the changed manifest.
evals.expected_output: Craft-skill acts as a thin authoring owner: it rechecks supplied baselines, writes only approved adapter files, validates manual frontmatter and required sections, and returns the exact changed manifest without taking adapter semantics or approval authority.
assertions: The response accepts the complete caller-owned adapter tuple without broadening it
Only the approved root and manifest are writable
Eligibility, naming, approval, proof semantics, product repair, and shipping stay with the wrapper
The result contains the exact changed manifest and validation result

evals.prompt: /skill:maintain-surface-verification-adapter passes one exact existing adapter URI/digest, owned file manifest, current baselines, preservation boundary, and re-drive recipe. One product file and one neighboring skill are outside the tuple.
evals.expected_output: Craft-skill preserves ownership: it may update only the existing adapter-owned files named in the tuple, leaves the product and neighboring skill unchanged, and cannot create a missing destination or reinterpret a product regression.
assertions: The existing adapter root and supplied baselines are rechecked before mutation
The product file, neighboring skill, and every unlisted path remain unchanged
A missing adapter destination is blocked rather than created
The wrapper retains maintenance classification and recipe-rebind authority
